desc: Derive a precise formula for the number of distinct in-degree sequences by analyzing the mapping from (x,y) to d.
Model the problem as a polynomial product where each position contributes a local generating function based on s_i.
Reduce the problem to a coefficient extraction problem in a product of polynomials (one per vertex) and identify the transfer matrix size.
Use NTT to multiply the polynomials efficiently in O(N log N).
Sum the coefficients that correspond to valid cycle closures.
Handle the global constraint on d_N (which depends on sum of y_i) by either including it in the polynomial or computing it separately.
Implement the solution in Python with careful attention to the modulus 998244353 (NTT-friendly prime).
